**Summary:**

The global food system faces unprecedented pressure as the world population is projected to reach 9.7 billion by 2050, requiring a 60% increase in production while climate change simultaneously reduces crop yields. Agriculture contributes roughly 25% of greenhouse gas emissions and exacerbates resource depletion—water scarcity threatens critical aquifers like the Ogallala, and soil degradation has reduced the productivity of 33% of arable land, while one-third of all food is lost or wasted. Proposed solutions include precision agriculture, vertical farming, alternative proteins, drought-resistant crops, and regenerative farming practices, supported by policy changes around subsidies and carbon pricing. The challenge lies in implementing these solutions at scale while maintaining affordability and accessibility for the world's poorest populations.
